content.text:
Yes—it’s hanging.

The prior cancelled run confirms the exact stuck test:

`system::history::describe_command::windows_job::tests::job_ends_descendants_after_the_shell_exits`

The shared cause is the Windows fixture:

```text
start "" /B ping -n 30 127.0.0.1
```

The tests assume `start /B` detaches and `cmd.exe` exits promptly. On the Actions runner it does not:

- `command_lifecycle...` takes roughly 33 seconds, hits the 30-second timeout, and fails because it expected the 2-second “kept output open” error.
- `job_ends_descendants...` then blocks indefinitely at `child.wait()` because it has no timeout.

The [current job](https://github.com/jdx/mise/actions/runs/34144734233/job/101814241727?pr=12918) was still in `cargo test` at 17:15 UTC, after starting that step at 16:52. Its retry wrapper will terminate the attempt after 30 minutes, although the job’s 40-minute outer timeout may interrupt the retry.

The fix should replace that unreliable detached-process fixture and also bound `child.wait()` so a regression fails instead of wedging CI.

I’ll patch PR #12918 in an isolated worktree so the unrelated edits in your current checkout stay untouched. I’ll make the Windows lifecycle tests time-bounded, reproduce as closely as this host allows, run focused checks, then push the fix to the PR branch.
